scope: Official Anthropic docs only (docs.claude.com / docs.anthropic.com / platform.claude.com prompting best-practices and per-model pages for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5). Look them up now; do not answer from memory.
Compare against packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/ (root and specialist sections) and packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/requirements.md if present, read-only.

result:
result: Each model has its own official guide, and none says "Respond tersely". The 5.5 guides do not cover conciseness, and the nearest wording is on the Opus 5 page. The claude-5.5 set already follows most of the 5.5 guidance, and I found six gaps (G1 to G6, listed below).

changed: none (read-only)

blockers: none

questions: none

notes:
- The user request is to drop the ban on stopping or steering running agents, with exceptions. That ban is in the repo at `packages/runtime/src/instructions/requirements.md` R-WAKE ("no polling ..., steering or stopping of running specialists") and at `claude-5.5/root/dispatch.md:9` ("no polling, steering or stopping ... a new user message leaves running specialists alone"). I did not check other model sets or `assignments.md:14`. No Anthropic guide supports or opposes the ban (inference).
- The Opus 5.5 page says its Opus 5 prompts "remain a reasonable starting point", so the Opus 5 conciseness and scope text applies to 5.5 by inference.
- The Opus 5 page says to remove explicit verification instructions. The Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 pages say to require a real check before "done". The repo follows the Sonnet and Haiku pages (`instruction-guidelines.md:13`). This conflicts across models, and I treat it as a choice for the root, not a gap.
- Not applicable to this set: the guidance on `thinking`/`effort` API settings, `display:"updates"`, structured JSON output, chatbot system-prompt adherence, multiapp exploration, pasted-text tags, visual crop tools and safeguard refusals.

Sourced facts (guide URLs and quotes):
- Shared page: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices. It has a per-model table: "Each of these models has its own prompting page."
- Opus 5.5 guide: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5-5
- Sonnet 5.5 guide: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-sonnet-5-5
- Haiku 5.5 guide: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-haiku-5-5
- Terse wording, Opus 5 page (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5):
  - Section "Response length and verbosity", for a user-facing multi-turn product: "Keep responses focused, brief, and concise. Keep disclaimers and caveats short, and spend most of the response on the main answer. When asked to explain something, give a high-level summary unless an in-depth explanation is specifically requested."
  - The same section, for a long system prompt, a reminder near the end: `<tone_preference>Keep outputs reasonably concise.</tone_preference>`
  - Section "User-facing progress updates": "Before your first tool call, say in one sentence what you're about to do. While working, give a brief update only when you find something important or change direction. When you finish, lead with the outcome ..."
  - Section "Written deliverable length": "Match the length of written documents to what the task needs: cover the substance, but do not pad with filler sections, redundant summaries, or boilerplate."
  - Shared page, section "Migrating away from prefilled responses": "Respond directly without preamble. Do not start with phrases like 'Here is...', 'Based on...', etc."
  - Shared page, section "Communication style and verbosity": Opus 5 "default user-facing responses run longer than prior models'" and "Prompt explicitly for conciseness instead."
  - Placement: every one of these goes in the system prompt. The 5.5 pages themselves have no length or conciseness instruction.
- Opus 5.5 page, section "Prompts written for thinking disabled": "a system prompt line such as 'Answer directly without deliberating.' can reduce thinking". The Haiku 5.5 page says "telling the model in the prompt to answer directly didn't stop it from thinking."

Gaps, with the file each would go in. G1 to G5 are inference; G6 is a sourced mismatch.

- G1. Not followed: the Opus 5.5 "Unattended agentic runs" guidance. It says an unattended agent "stops partway through a long task after reporting progress", and the fix is to name the early stops to avoid and the ones to keep.
  - `instruction-guidelines.md:12` does this only for specialist briefs.
  - Nothing tells the root not to end its own turn on a summary that announces the next step or on an offer to wait.
  - Belongs in `root/user-messages.md` or `root/task-list.md`.
- G2. Not followed: Sonnet 5.5 "Open-ended requests": "When the user asks for ideas, options or a plan, give them that and stop. Don't start building or changing anything until they say to go ahead."
  - It appears only in the brief guideline at `instruction-guidelines.md:12`, not as a rule for the root's own turns.
  - Belongs in `root/user-messages.md`.
- G3. Not followed: Opus 5 "Written deliverable length" ("do not pad with filler sections, redundant summaries, or boilerplate").
  - `specialist/writing-bar.md` covers instruction text only, and `pr-text.md` covers PR text.
  - Belongs in `specialist/writing-bar.md` (inference: it applies to Opus 5.5).
- G4. Not followed: Opus 5 "Task scope": "If the request seems mistaken or a better approach exists, say so in a sentence and continue with the task as asked ... Make routine judgment calls yourself, and check in only when different readings of the request would lead to materially different work."
  - `specialist/scope.md` partly covers this. The "say so in a sentence and continue" part is absent.
  - Belongs in `specialist/scope.md`.
- G5. Not followed: Opus 5.5 "Time signals for multiagent harnesses". It suggests an elapsed-time budget line, or "Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better."
  - It appears nowhere in the set.
  - It is optional and has a quality trade-off, so treat it as a design choice.
  - Would go in `root/workflows.md` or `root/dispatch.md`.
- G6. Not followed: the Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 "User-facing progress updates" guidance. It says to state intent in one sentence before the first tool call and give a short recap.
  - It conflicts by design with R-TASKLIST and `user-messages.md`, which say not to narrate progress.
  - The user wants terse output, so keep the repo rule. This is a recorded deviation, not a gap to close.

Already followed, no gap:
- Keep-working and stop-and-report: `specialist/scope.md:6`, `instruction-guidelines.md:12`.
- A real check before "done": `specialist/working.md`.
- Look up facts that may have changed, and avoid blanket search instructions: `instruction-guidelines.md:14`.
- Do not ask for reasoning in the reply, and no "think less" lines: `instruction-guidelines.md:10-11`.
- Delegation, parallel calls and pasted-content-as-data rules.
- Calm positive phrasing and examples.
- Answer first: `root/user-messages.md:3` ("Be terse: answer first.") and `specialist/report.md`.
